northpoints: Make full-fidelity testing fast enough to run continuously, not only at release time.
Make browser-extension verification prove the exact loaded build, runtime identity, background/content behavior, diagnostics, restart and persistence.
Grow Ferrum into one app-testing control plane for web, browser extensions, Electron, processes/services and native/mobile apps.
Make agent control low-latency and deterministic first, with semantic recovery as a visible fallback rather than hidden magic.
Improve Ferrum whenever real GameSync or other app testing exposes avoidable slowness, missing observability, flaky control or unsupported workflows.
guardrails: Never trade test coverage, data, fidelity, diagnostics or supported target behavior for speed.
Chromium-specific and extension-specific behavior requires a real Chromium fidelity lane even when Lightpanda or another fast lane also passes.
Every visible control and CLI command must be wired to a real implementation path.
A success claim requires an evidence bundle, not a UI state or log message.
Past Ferrum prototypes are not canonical implementation sources.
acceptanceSignals: GameSync can be built, loaded, exercised, restarted and diagnosed in Ferrum with exact build identity.
Ferrum self-tests pass on Linux and Windows Chromium.
A single test-spec model covers browser and non-browser application targets.
Agent operations can use compact snapshots and MCP without sacrificing deterministic selectors and direct actions.
Measured Ferrum performance improves over time on fixed workloads without reducing scope.
